audio.name: Audio
audio.description: Validated Audio registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: System Beep Driver
entries.description: This affects the old system beep behavior driven by the Beep driver. Most people will never notice it unless they are cleaning up legacy system sounds or debugging old compatibility behavior.

presets.label: System start (observed baseline)
presets.description: Loaded by the I/O subsystem. The guest probe restored this value as the baseline on Win25H2Clean.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: The service is disabled and will not be loaded. The current app writes 4 here to disable the Beep driver.

entries.name: Show Disconnected Audio Devices
entries.description: This makes disconnected audio devices appear in the classic Sound control panel. It is mainly useful for troubleshooting, advanced audio setup, or cleaning up stale devices.

presets.label: Hide disconnected audio devices
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that the classic Sound control panel reads ShowDisconnectedDevices = 0 on this build. This is the observed off state for the preference.

presets.label: Show disconnected audio devices
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that the classic Sound control panel reads ShowDisconnectedDevices = 1 on this build. This is the observed show-disconnected state used by the app.

entries.name: Show Hidden Audio Devices
entries.description: This makes hidden audio devices appear in the classic Sound control panel. It is mainly useful for troubleshooting, advanced audio setup, or driver cleanup.

presets.label: Hide hidden audio devices
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that the classic Sound control panel reads ShowHiddenDevices = 0 on this build. This is the observed off state for the preference.

presets.label: Show hidden audio devices
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that the classic Sound control panel reads ShowHiddenDevices = 1 on this build. This is the observed show-hidden state used by the app.

developer.name: Developer
developer.description: Validated Developer registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: .NET CLI Telemetry Opt-Out
entries.description: The .NET SDK and CLI can send telemetry about tool usage. This tweak sets the current user's opt-out environment variable so new .NET CLI sessions stop sending that telemetry.

presets.label: .NET CLI telemetry opted out
presets.description: The .NET CLI telemetry is opted out for the current user.

presets.label: .NET CLI telemetry opted out
presets.description: The .NET CLI telemetry is opted out for the current user.

entries.name: Windows Long Paths
entries.description: Windows can remove the old 260-character path limit. That helps many compatible applications, especially developer tools and projects with very deep folder trees.

entries.name: Global Node.js Memory Limit Override
entries.description: This tweak makes Node.js start with a larger memory limit by default. It can help very large builds or monorepos, but it also makes Node processes use more memory budget.

entries.name: PowerShell Script Execution Policy
entries.description: PowerShell execution policy controls which scripts are allowed to run. RemoteSigned allows local scripts and requires downloaded scripts to be signed.

presets.label: Allow local scripts and remote signed scripts
presets.description: PowerShell allows local scripts and requires remote scripts to be signed.

presets.label: Only signed scripts
presets.description: PowerShell requires all scripts to be signed.

presets.label: All scripts allowed
presets.description: PowerShell allows scripts without the RemoteSigned restriction.

entries.name: Enable Windows Long Paths for Python Workflows
entries.description: Some Python environments fail on Windows when project folders get very deep. Enabling Windows long paths removes the old 260-character path limit for compatible applications, including Python workflows that rely on the operating system long-path setting.

presets.label: Long paths disabled
presets.description: Win32 long-path support is not enabled through this registry setting.

presets.label: Long paths enabled
presets.description: Long-path-aware applications, including Python workflows that rely on the Windows long-path setting, can access paths beyond the normal 260-character limit.

entries.name: Windows Developer Mode
entries.description: Developer Mode turns on Windows support for building, sideloading, and debugging apps. Most casual users do not need it, but developers often do.

explorer.name: Explorer
explorer.description: Validated Explorer registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Always Show Icons, Never Thumbnails
entries.description: Explorer can show file icons instead of generating thumbnails.

presets.label: Allow thumbnails
presets.description: Explorer allows thumbnail previews instead of forcing icons only. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, the 25H2 default-user hive sets IconsOnly = 0, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

presets.label: Always show icons, never thumbnails
presets.description: Explorer forces icons instead of thumbnails. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

entries.name: Low Disk Space Warning
entries.description: Windows can warn you when a drive is running low on space. People sometimes turn these warnings off on lab machines or kiosk-like systems, but most users should keep them on.

entries.name: Taskbar Chat Icon
entries.description: Windows 11 can show a Chat icon on the taskbar. People often hide it when they do not use Chat or want a cleaner taskbar.

presets.label: Show
presets.description: The Chat icon is shown on the taskbar by default, and users can still show or hide it in Settings.

presets.label: Hide
presets.description: The Chat icon is hidden by default, and users can still show or hide it in Settings. This is the state the app now applies.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: The Chat icon is not displayed and users cannot show or hide it in Settings.

entries.name: Enable Explorer Compact View
entries.description: Explorer compact view reduces spacing between items so more files fit on screen. Some users like the denser layout, while others prefer the roomier default view.

presets.label: Compact view disabled
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that Explorer.EXE queries UseCompactMode = 0 on shell restart. This is the observed non-compact state on this build.

presets.label: Compact view enabled
presets.description: Procmon confirmed that Explorer.EXE queries UseCompactMode = 1 on shell restart. This is the observed compact-view state used by the app.

entries.name: Hide Empty Drives
entries.description: Explorer can hide or show drives that do not currently have media present.

presets.label: Show empty drives
presets.description: Explorer keeps drives with no media visible. The Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart into This PC.

presets.label: Hide empty drives
presets.description: Explorer hides drives with no media present. The Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart into This PC.

entries.name: Launch Folder Windows in a Separate Process
entries.description: Explorer can run folder windows in the same process or split them into separate Explorer processes.

presets.label: Use the default shared Explorer process model
presets.description: Folder windows are not forced into separate Explorer processes. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, the 25H2 default hive exports SeparateProcess = 0, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

presets.label: Launch folder windows in a separate process
presets.description: Explorer uses the separate-process mode for folder windows. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

entries.name: Show Compressed and Encrypted Files in Color
entries.description: File Explorer can color compressed and encrypted NTFS items so they stand out visually.

presets.label: Color compressed and encrypted files
presets.description: Explorer uses the special color cue for compressed and encrypted NTFS files. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, the 25H2 default hive exports ShowCompColor = 1, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

presets.label: Do not color compressed and encrypted files
presets.description: Explorer does not use the special color cue for compressed and encrypted NTFS files. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

entries.name: Show Drive Letters First
entries.description: Explorer can show drive letters ahead of the drive name, or leave that presentation disabled.

presets.label: Do not show drive letters first
presets.description: Explorer does not enable the drive-letter-first presentation. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

presets.label: Show drive letters first
presets.description: Explorer enables the drive-letter-first presentation. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

entries.name: Show File Extensions
entries.description: File Explorer can hide or show file extensions like .txt, .zip, or .exe. Many advanced users prefer to always see them.

presets.label: Hide file extensions
presets.description: Explorer hides known file extensions. In the runtime capture, Explorer consumed HideFileExt = 1 after restart and Shell.Application rendered the test file as alpha.

presets.label: Show file extensions
presets.description: Explorer displays known file extensions. In the runtime capture, Explorer consumed HideFileExt = 0 after restart and Shell.Application rendered the test file as alpha.txt.

entries.name: Show Full Path in Explorer
entries.description: Explorer can show the full folder path instead of a shorter title. Some advanced users prefer that when they navigate deep directories.

presets.label: Do not show full path
presets.description: Explorer does not display the full path in the title bar.

presets.label: Show full path
presets.description: Explorer displays the full path in the title bar.

entries.name: Show Hidden Files and Folders
entries.description: File Explorer can show or hide files and folders marked with the hidden attribute. Power users often enable this to inspect more of the filesystem.

presets.label: Hide hidden files and folders
presets.description: Explorer hides items marked with the hidden attribute. In the runtime capture, Explorer consumed Hidden = 2 after restart and the Explorer UI listed only visible.txt.

presets.label: Show hidden files and folders
presets.description: Explorer shows items marked with the hidden attribute. In the runtime capture, Explorer consumed Hidden = 1 after restart and the Explorer UI listed both ghost.txt and visible.txt.

entries.name: Show Explorer Info Tips
entries.description: File Explorer can show or suppress pop-up descriptions for folder and desktop items when you hover them.

presets.label: Show Explorer info tips
presets.description: Explorer info-tip pop-ups are enabled. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, the 25H2 default hive exports ShowInfoTip = 1, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

presets.label: Hide Explorer info tips
presets.description: Explorer info-tip pop-ups are disabled. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

entries.name: Show Protected Operating System Files
entries.description: File Explorer can hide or reveal protected operating system files. Most people should leave them hidden, but advanced troubleshooting sometimes requires seeing them.

presets.label: Hide protected operating system files
presets.description: Protected operating system files stay hidden. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, the 25H2 default hive exports ShowSuperHidden = 0, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

presets.label: Show protected operating system files
presets.description: Protected operating system files become visible. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

entries.name: Show Recent Items In Home
entries.description: Explorer Home can show or hide recently used files.

presets.label: Do not show recent items
presets.description: Explorer does not show recently used files in Home. The Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

presets.label: Show recent items
presets.description: Explorer shows recently used files in Home. The Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

entries.name: Show Status Bar
entries.description: Explorer can show or hide its status bar at the bottom of the window.

presets.label: Show status bar
presets.description: Explorer shows the status bar. The 25H2 default-user hive sets ShowStatusBar = 1, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

presets.label: Hide status bar
presets.description: Explorer does not show the status bar. The Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

entries.name: Display File Icons On Thumbnails
entries.description: Explorer can show or hide file icons on top of thumbnails.

presets.label: Show file icons on thumbnails
presets.description: Explorer shows file icons on top of thumbnails. Microsoft documents 1 as the enabled state, the 25H2 default-user hive sets ShowTypeOverlay = 1, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 1 after restart.

presets.label: Do not show file icons on thumbnails
presets.description: Explorer does not show file icons on top of thumbnails. Microsoft documents 0 as the disabled state, and the Win25H2Clean Procmon capture shows Explorer.EXE querying Data: 0 after restart.

entries.name: Taskbar Alignment
entries.description: Windows 11 can keep the taskbar icons centered or move them to the left. Some people prefer the older left-aligned layout.

presets.label: Left aligned
presets.description: Taskbar icons and the Start button are aligned to the left. Procmon confirmed Explorer.EXE queries TaskbarAl = 0 after the value is written and Explorer restarts.

presets.label: Center aligned
presets.description: Taskbar icons are centered. Procmon confirmed Explorer.EXE queries TaskbarAl = 1 after the value is written and Explorer restarts.

network.name: Network
network.description: Validated Network registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: NCSI Active Probing Policy
entries.description: Windows checks internet connectivity by making active test requests. Turning those tests off can change how Windows decides whether a network has internet access.

presets.label: Policy disabled
presets.description: The policy is disabled, so the normal active-test behavior remains available.

presets.label: Disable active probing
presets.description: NCSI does not run the active tests Microsoft describes.

entries.name: IPv6 Stack Disable Override
entries.description: IPv6 is the newer network protocol stack that Windows expects to have available. Turning it off can break some network features even if a home network mostly feels like IPv4.

presets.label: IPv6 enabled
presets.description: All IPv6 components are enabled.

presets.label: Prefer IPv4 over IPv6
presets.description: Windows keeps IPv6 available but prefers IPv4 in prefix policies.

presets.label: Disable IPv6 except loopback
presets.description: All IPv6 interfaces except loopback are disabled.

entries.name: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR)
entries.description: LLMNR lets Windows ask nearby devices for names on the local subnet when normal DNS does not help. Modern networks often disable it, but it can still help in some small or legacy local networks.

presets.label: LLMNR disabled
presets.description: The policy is enabled and multicast name resolution is turned off.

presets.label: LLMNR enabled
presets.description: The policy is disabled and multicast name resolution is allowed.

entries.name: Set mDNS Policy to Local Settings
entries.description: mDNS is a local-network name resolution protocol used by some discovery and service-advertising workflows. This policy setting disables the explicit mDNS policy so Windows falls back to its locally configured mDNS behavior.

presets.label: Policy disabled
presets.description: The policy is disabled, which Microsoft describes as returning to locally configured settings rather than publishing a hard off state.

presets.label: Policy enabled
presets.description: The DNS client uses mDNS because the policy is enabled.

entries.name: DNS Client NetBIOS Name Resolution
entries.description: Windows can use NetBIOS-style name resolution through the DNS client policy layer. This policy lets you fully disable it, allow it, or choose more limited modes.

presets.label: Disable
presets.description: Disable NetBIOS name resolution for the DNS client policy.

presets.label: Allow
presets.description: Allow NetBIOS name resolution.

presets.label: Disable on public networks
presets.description: Disable NetBIOS name resolution on public networks only.

presets.label: Learning mode
presets.description: Use the learning mode defined by the DNS client policy.

entries.name: Plaintext SMB Passwords
entries.description: This setting decides whether Windows is willing to send an unencrypted password to certain old SMB servers. Modern systems should almost never need that behavior.

presets.label: Do not send plaintext passwords
presets.description: Windows does not send unencrypted passwords to third-party SMB servers.

presets.label: Allow plaintext passwords
presets.description: Windows can send unencrypted passwords to third-party SMB servers.

entries.name: Smart Multi-Homed Name Resolution
entries.description: When a PC has multiple network paths, Windows can try name lookups more aggressively across them. This policy decides whether that smart multi-homed behavior stays on.

presets.label: Feature enabled
presets.description: The policy is disabled and smart multi-homed name resolution remains on.

presets.label: Feature disabled
presets.description: The policy is enabled and smart multi-homed name resolution is turned off.

entries.name: SMBv1 Server Protocol Support
entries.description: SMB is the file-sharing protocol Windows uses for network shares. SMBv1 is the old version. Modern systems should avoid it, but some very old devices still need it.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: The SMBv1 server protocol is disabled for LanmanServer.

presets.label: Enabled
presets.description: The SMBv1 server protocol is enabled for LanmanServer.

entries.name: SMBv2 and SMBv3 Server Protocol Support
entries.description: SMBv2 and SMBv3 are the modern Windows file-sharing protocols. Turning them off forces the machine away from the normal modern SMB stack.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: The SMBv2 and SMBv3 server protocols are disabled.

presets.label: Enabled
presets.description: The SMBv2 and SMBv3 server protocols are enabled explicitly.

entries.name: Wi-Fi Sense Suggested Hotspot Policy
entries.description: This controls whether Windows can automatically connect to suggested open hotspots, contact-shared networks, and some paid hotspot discovery flows.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: Suggested hotspot, shared-network, and paid service options are turned off and users cannot enable them.

presets.label: Enabled or user-allowed
presets.description: The policy allows users to choose whether to use these features.

entries.name: LLTD Responder Driver Policy
entries.description: The LLTD Responder lets other PCs discover this device on the local network during Windows network mapping and related discovery tasks.

presets.label: Policy disabled
presets.description: The administrative template policy is disabled, which falls back to default LLTD Responder behavior.

presets.label: Policy enabled
presets.description: The LLTD Responder is explicitly turned on by policy.

entries.name: LLTD Mapper I/O Driver Policy
entries.description: LLTD helps Windows map and discover devices on a local network. The Mapper I/O side lets the PC ask the network about its topology.

presets.label: Policy disabled
presets.description: The administrative template policy is disabled, which reverts to default LLTD Mapper I/O behavior rather than publishing a hard feature-off state.

presets.label: Policy enabled
presets.description: The LLTD Mapper I/O driver is explicitly turned on by policy.

entries.name: IPv4 Preference Override
entries.description: This keeps IPv6 available but tells Windows to prefer IPv4 when both protocols can work.

presets.label: No preference override
presets.description: IPv6 is enabled with the normal default preference behavior.

presets.label: Prefer IPv4
presets.description: Windows prefers IPv4 over IPv6 in prefix policies while leaving IPv6 enabled.

presets.label: Disable IPv6 except loopback
presets.description: This is a stronger override that disables IPv6 components instead of merely preferring IPv4.

entries.name: Require NTLM SSP Client Session Security and 128-bit Encryption
entries.description: This setting raises the minimum session security requirements for NTLM SSP based clients. In the app's enabled state it requires both NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption.

presets.label: No extra minimum flags
presets.description: No additional NTLM session security minimum is forced through this value.

presets.label: Require NTLMv2 session security
presets.description: Require NTLMv2 session security for NTLM SSP based clients.

presets.label: Require 128-bit encryption
presets.description: Require 128-bit encryption for NTLM SSP based clients.

presets.label: Require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption
presets.description: Require both NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption for NTLM SSP based clients.

entries.name: SMB Client Large MTU
entries.description: Large MTU lets SMB send larger requests over the network. On modern Windows networks this usually helps file-copy and share performance.

presets.label: Large MTU enabled
presets.description: Large MTU support stays enabled for SMB client connections.

presets.label: Large MTU disabled
presets.description: Large MTU is turned off and SMB uses smaller request sizing behavior.

entries.name: SMB Server Encryption Requirement
entries.description: SMB encryption protects file-sharing traffic so other systems on the network cannot easily read it in transit. Turning this on at the server level makes the machine stricter about how its shared data is accessed.

presets.label: Global encryption not required
presets.description: The server does not force global SMB encryption through this registry override.

presets.label: Global encryption required
presets.description: The server requires SMB encryption for shared data through this registry override.

entries.name: SMB Server Reject Unencrypted Access
entries.description: This setting makes the SMB server reject clients that try to access shares without encryption. It is stricter than simply preferring safer behavior because noncompliant clients are actively refused.

presets.label: Do not reject unencrypted access
presets.description: The server does not force this global rejection rule through the registry override.

presets.label: Reject unencrypted access
presets.description: The server rejects clients that do not use SMB encryption through this registry override.

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: Validated Notifications registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Windows Feedback Request Frequency
entries.description: Windows can occasionally ask for feedback. This tweak sets a user preference intended to reduce or stop those requests.

entries.name: Lock Screen Toast Notifications
entries.description: Windows can show some app notifications directly on the lock screen. This policy decides whether apps can raise those lock-screen toast alerts for the current user.

presets.label: Lock-screen toasts allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and apps can still raise toast notifications on the lock screen.

presets.label: Lock-screen toasts turned off
presets.description: Applications cannot raise toast notifications on the lock screen.

entries.name: Notification Mirroring
entries.description: Windows can mirror some notifications to other devices. This policy decides whether that cross-device mirroring is allowed for the current user.

presets.label: Notification mirroring allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and notifications can still be mirrored to other devices.

presets.label: Notification mirroring turned off
presets.description: Notifications are not mirrored to other devices for the current user.

entries.name: Tile Notifications
entries.description: Tile notifications are the live updates and badges some Windows tiles can show. This policy decides whether those tile updates are allowed for the current user.

presets.label: Tile notifications allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and applications can still update tiles and tile badges.

presets.label: Tile notifications turned off
presets.description: Applications and system features cannot update tiles and tile badges for the current user.

entries.name: Toast Notifications
entries.description: Toast notifications are the pop-up alerts apps show in Windows. This policy decides whether apps can raise those pop-ups for the current user.

presets.label: Toast notifications allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and apps can still raise toast notifications.

presets.label: Toast notifications turned off
presets.description: Applications cannot raise toast notifications for the current user.

performance.name: Performance
performance.description: Validated Performance registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Disable Window Animations
entries.description: Windows can animate windows when they open, close, minimize, or restore. Turning that off can make the interface feel snappier and reduce motion.

presets.label: Window animations disabled
presets.description: A local SPI_SETANIMATION runtime diff confirmed that disabling the official Win32 animation feature persists MinAnimate = "0" on this build.

presets.label: Window animations enabled
presets.description: A local SPI_SETANIMATION runtime diff confirmed that enabling the official Win32 animation feature persists MinAnimate = "1" on this build.

entries.name: Remove Menu Show Delay
entries.description: Windows can wait a short moment before showing some menus. Setting the delay lower can make menus feel faster and more immediate.

presets.label: Default-like menu delay
presets.description: A local SPI_SETMENUSHOWDELAY runtime diff confirmed that setting the official Win32 menu-delay feature to 400 persists MenuShowDelay = "400" on this build.

presets.label: No menu show delay
presets.description: A local SPI_SETMENUSHOWDELAY runtime diff confirmed that setting the official Win32 menu-delay feature to 0 persists MenuShowDelay = "0" on this build.

policy.name: Policy
policy.description: Stable policy-backed registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Enable Virtualization
entries.description: Enable Virtualization controls legacy UAC file and registry virtualization under the Policies\System branch.

presets.label: Observed baseline
presets.description: Enables legacy file and registry virtualization for qualifying legacy apps.

presets.label: Virtualization off
presets.description: Disables legacy file and registry virtualization.

power.name: Power
power.description: Stable raw power-manager registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Allow Audio To Enable Execution Required Power Requests
entries.description: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to whether active audio can enable execution-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.

entries.name: Allow System Required Power Requests
entries.description: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to how the power manager treats system-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.

entries.name: Class1 Initial Unpark Count
entries.description: Class1 Initial Unpark Count is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

entries.name: Hiber File Size Percent
entries.description: Hiber File Size Percent is a low-level power-manager value under the main Power key that appears to relate to hibernation file sizing behavior.

entries.name: Lid Reliability State
entries.description: Lid Reliability State is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

entries.name: MF Buffering Threshold
entries.description: MF Buffering Threshold is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

entries.name: Perf Calculate Actual Utilization
entries.description: Perf Calculate Actual Utilization is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

entries.name: Power Request Override Subtree
entries.description: This is a low-level Control\Power subtree that appears to back override handling for power requests.

entries.name: Timer Rebase Threshold On Drips Exit
entries.description: Timer Rebase Threshold On Drips Exit is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

entries.name: Session Manager Watchdog Timeouts
entries.description: These values appear to control watchdog timeout behavior around directed power transitions. They are not normal user-facing power options and are being tracked as a low-level research lane rather than a supported tweak.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.description: Validated Privacy registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Microsoft Accounts on This Device
entries.description: Windows can let people add Microsoft accounts or sign in with them on the device. This security option controls whether Microsoft accounts are allowed, partly blocked, or fully blocked.

presets.label: Microsoft accounts allowed
presets.description: The security option is disabled and users can add or sign in with Microsoft accounts normally.

presets.label: Block adding new Microsoft accounts
presets.description: Users cannot add new Microsoft accounts, but the stronger sign-in block is not enforced.

presets.label: Block adding and signing in with Microsoft accounts
presets.description: Users cannot add Microsoft accounts and cannot sign in with them on the device.

entries.name: Disable Advertising ID
entries.description: Windows uses an advertising ID so apps can personalize experiences across apps. Turning it off stops apps from using that ID for cross-app personalization.

presets.label: Policy not turning it off
presets.description: The policy is disabled and users can still control whether apps use the advertising ID.

presets.label: Advertising ID turned off by policy
presets.description: Apps cannot use the advertising ID for experiences across apps.

entries.name: App Diagnostic Information Access
entries.description: Some Windows apps can request diagnostic information about other apps. This policy decides whether apps are user-controlled, always allowed, or always denied.

presets.label: User is in control
presets.description: The user decides whether Windows apps can access diagnostic information about other apps.

presets.label: Force allow
presets.description: Windows apps are allowed to access diagnostic information about other apps and the user cannot change it.

presets.label: Force deny
presets.description: Windows apps are not allowed to access diagnostic information about other apps and the user cannot change it.

entries.name: App Launch Tracking
entries.description: Windows can track which apps you launch so Start and Search can personalize some results. People turn it off when they want less app-usage tracking.

entries.name: App Suggestions in Start
entries.description: Windows can suggest promoted apps and related content in places like the Start menu. People often turn this off when they want a cleaner Start experience.

entries.name: Application Compatibility Telemetry
entries.description: Windows can collect anonymous telemetry about how applications use certain system components so compatibility systems can learn from it. This policy decides whether that telemetry engine runs.

presets.label: Application Telemetry turned off
presets.description: The Application Telemetry engine is turned off for the device.

presets.label: Application Telemetry allowed
presets.description: This policy does not turn the Application Telemetry engine off.

entries.name: Background App Execution
entries.description: Windows apps can keep running in the background to sync, refresh notifications, or finish work. This policy decides whether users control that, all apps are allowed, or all apps are denied.

presets.label: User is in control
presets.description: The user decides whether Windows apps can run in the background.

presets.label: Force allow
presets.description: Windows apps are allowed to run in the background and the user cannot change it.

presets.label: Force deny
presets.description: Windows apps are not allowed to run in the background and the user cannot change it.

entries.name: Windows Biometrics
entries.description: Windows can use fingerprint, face, or other biometric features for sign-in and related capabilities. This device policy controls whether biometrics are allowed at all.

presets.label: Biometrics disabled
presets.description: Biometric features are disabled by policy.

presets.label: Biometrics enabled
presets.description: Biometric features are explicitly allowed by policy.

entries.name: Biometric Sign-in for Domain Accounts
entries.description: Windows can let domain users sign in with biometrics when the device and domain setup support it. This policy controls whether domain accounts are allowed to use that biometric sign-in path.

presets.label: Domain biometric sign-in disabled
presets.description: Domain accounts cannot use biometric sign-in through this policy path.

presets.label: Domain biometric sign-in enabled
presets.description: Domain accounts are allowed to use biometric sign-in through this policy path.

entries.name: Biometric Sign-in
entries.description: Windows can let users sign in with biometrics like fingerprint or face through the credential provider. This policy controls whether that sign-in path is available.

presets.label: Biometric sign-in disabled
presets.description: Users cannot sign in with biometrics through the credential provider.

presets.label: Biometric sign-in enabled
presets.description: Biometric sign-in is allowed through the credential provider.

entries.name: Camera Device Use
entries.description: Windows can allow or block the use of camera devices on the machine. This policy decides whether cameras are usable at all.

presets.label: Camera disabled
presets.description: Camera devices are disabled by policy.

presets.label: Camera allowed
presets.description: Camera devices are explicitly allowed by policy.

entries.name: Cloud Consumer Account State Content
entries.description: Some Windows experiences can use cloud-backed consumer account state content. This policy decides whether those experiences may use that content or must fall back to default content instead.

presets.label: Cloud consumer content allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and Windows experiences may use cloud consumer account state content.

presets.label: Cloud consumer content disabled
presets.description: Windows experiences using this client component fall back to default content instead.

entries.name: Windows Copilot
entries.description: Windows Copilot is the built-in AI assistant experience in Windows. This policy decides whether that experience is available to the signed-in user.

presets.label: Copilot turned off
presets.description: The user cannot use Windows Copilot, and the Copilot icon does not appear on the taskbar.

presets.label: Copilot allowed
presets.description: This policy does not turn Copilot off, so the user can use Copilot when it is available to them.

entries.name: Cross-Device Experiences Machine Policy
entries.description: Windows can let devices belonging to the same user discover each other and continue some experiences across devices. This policy controls the official machine-level part of that feature.

presets.label: Continue experiences blocked
presets.description: The device is not discoverable by other devices and cannot participate in cross-device experiences.

presets.label: Continue experiences allowed
presets.description: The device can participate in cross-device experiences.

entries.name: Device Name in Diagnostic Data
entries.description: Windows diagnostic data can include the computer name. This policy decides whether that name is allowed to be sent with diagnostic data.

presets.label: Do not include device name
presets.description: The device name is blocked from diagnostic data by policy.

presets.label: Include device name
presets.description: The device name is explicitly allowed in diagnostic data by policy.

entries.name: Diagnostic Data Deletion
entries.description: Windows can offer a Settings action that deletes diagnostic data associated with the device. This policy decides whether that delete option is available.

presets.label: Diagnostic data deletion allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and the delete option remains available.

presets.label: Diagnostic data deletion disabled
presets.description: The delete option is blocked by policy.

entries.name: Diagnostic Data Viewer
entries.description: Windows includes a viewer that can show diagnostic data categories on the device. This policy decides whether that viewer is available.

presets.label: Diagnostic Data Viewer allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and the viewer remains available.

presets.label: Diagnostic Data Viewer disabled
presets.description: The viewer is blocked by policy.

entries.name: Microsoft Feedback Notifications
entries.description: Windows can occasionally show prompts asking for feedback. This policy decides whether those feedback questions appear on the device.

presets.label: Feedback notifications allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and Windows feedback prompts may be shown.

presets.label: Feedback notifications disabled
presets.description: Windows feedback prompts are blocked by policy.

entries.name: File History
entries.description: File History is Windows' built-in feature for making regular automatic backups of personal files. This policy decides whether File History can be turned on.

presets.label: File History allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and File History can be activated for regular automatic backups.

presets.label: File History disabled
presets.description: File History cannot be activated to create regular automatic backups.

entries.name: Find My Device
entries.description: Find My Device can register the device and its location in the cloud so it can be located later. This policy decides whether that feature is allowed.

presets.label: Find My Device enabled
presets.description: The device and its location can be registered in the cloud so the feature can locate the device later.

presets.label: Find My Device disabled
presets.description: The device and its location are not registered and Find My Device will not work.

entries.name: Online Font Providers
entries.description: Windows can contact an online font provider to download font catalog data and, when needed, font data for rendering text. This policy decides whether that online font path is allowed.

presets.label: Online font providers disabled
presets.description: Windows does not connect to an online font provider and only enumerates locally installed fonts.

presets.label: Online font providers enabled
presets.description: Windows can query an online font provider for catalog and font data when needed.

entries.name: KMS Client Online AVS Validation
entries.description: Windows can send KMS client activation-state data to Microsoft during activation. This policy decides whether that data is sent automatically.

presets.label: KMS activation data sent automatically
presets.description: The policy is disabled and KMS client activation data is automatically sent to Microsoft.

presets.label: KMS activation data not sent automatically
presets.description: The policy is enabled and the computer opts out of automatically sending KMS client activation data to Microsoft.

entries.name: Website Access to Language List
entries.description: Windows can let websites use your language list to show locally relevant content. This setting controls whether that language-list access is allowed.

entries.name: Security Questions for Local Accounts
entries.description: Windows can let local-account users create security questions so they can reset their password later. This policy decides whether those security questions are allowed.

presets.label: Security questions allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and local users can use security questions if the feature is otherwise available.

presets.label: Security questions blocked
presets.description: The policy is enabled and local users cannot set up or use security questions to reset their passwords.

entries.name: Location Consent Store (System)
entries.description: This changes the system-level location permission state to deny access.

presets.label: System-level allow
presets.description: The system-level runtime consent value explicitly allows device location access.

presets.label: System-level deny
presets.description: The current app writes a device-level deny state for location access.

entries.name: Location Scripting
entries.description: Some scripts and apps can access Windows location features through scripting interfaces. This policy decides whether that scripting access is allowed.

presets.label: Location scripting allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and scripted access to location remains allowed.

presets.label: Location scripting disabled
presets.description: Scripted access to location is blocked by policy.

entries.name: Location Feature
entries.description: Windows can provide location information to apps and system features. This policy decides whether the location feature is turned off for the computer.

presets.label: Location allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and programs are not prevented from using location information.

presets.label: Location turned off
presets.description: The location feature is turned off and programs on the computer are prevented from using location information from that feature.

entries.name: MDM Enrollment
entries.description: Windows can allow the computer to enroll into a Mobile Device Management service for remote management. This policy decides whether new MDM enrollment is allowed.

presets.label: MDM enrollment enabled
presets.description: The policy is disabled and MDM enrollment is allowed for all users.

presets.label: MDM enrollment disabled
presets.description: New MDM enrollment is disabled for all users on the device. Existing MDM enrollments aren't removed by this policy.

entries.name: Message Service Cloud Sync
entries.description: Windows can back up and restore cellular text messages through Microsoft's cloud services. This policy decides whether that cloud sync is allowed on the device.

presets.label: Message cloud sync disabled
presets.description: Backup and restore of cellular text messages to Microsoft's cloud services is blocked by policy.

presets.label: Message cloud sync allowed
presets.description: The device is allowed to use Microsoft's cloud backup and restore path for cellular messages.

entries.name: OneSettings Downloads
entries.description: Windows can periodically connect to the OneSettings service to download configuration settings. This policy decides whether those download attempts happen.

presets.label: Allow OneSettings downloads
presets.description: Windows can periodically attempt to connect to the OneSettings service to download configuration settings.

presets.label: Disable OneSettings downloads
presets.description: Windows will not attempt to connect to the OneSettings service.

entries.name: Online Tips in Settings
entries.description: The Settings app can contact Microsoft to retrieve tips and help content. This policy decides whether those online tips are allowed.

presets.label: Online tips disabled
presets.description: The Settings app won't retrieve online tips and help content.

presets.label: Online tips allowed
presets.description: The Settings app is allowed to retrieve online tips and help content.

entries.name: Disable PCA Compatibility Diagnostics Detection
entries.description: Windows PCA watches for compatibility issues when you run applications and drivers, and can show warnings or suggest fixes. This policy controls whether that detection runs. Disabling it stops PCA from actively monitoring for compatibility problems - it does not disable PCA itself (that is controlled separately by DisablePCA).

presets.label: Disable PCA diagnostics detection
presets.description: disabledValue in pca.admx. PCA does not detect compatibility issues. Detection and related diagnostics are suppressed. Note: has no effect if DisablePCA=1 is active.

presets.label: PCA diagnostics detection active (policy explicit)
presets.description: enabledValue in pca.admx. PCA detects compatibility issues. Equivalent to missing/not configured.

entries.name: Phone-PC Linking
entries.description: Windows can link the PC with a phone so reading, emailing, and similar tasks can continue across devices. This policy decides whether the PC can participate in that linking.

presets.label: Phone-PC linking disabled
presets.description: The device is not allowed to be linked to phones, removes itself from linked-phone device lists, and cannot participate in Continue on PC experiences.

presets.label: Phone-PC linking enabled
presets.description: The device can enroll in Phone-PC linking functionality and participate in Continue on PC experiences.

entries.name: Disable Program Compatibility Assistant
entries.description: Program Compatibility Assistant monitors applications and can suggest compatibility solutions when Windows detects install failures, runtime failures, or blocked drivers. This policy turns PCA off.

presets.label: Turn off Program Compatibility Assistant
presets.description: enabledValue in AppCompat.admx. PCA is turned off, so Windows will not present compatibility solutions for detected application issues. VM Procmon capture on 2026-03-26 in Win25H2Clean confirmed powershell.exe writes DisablePCA=REG_DWORD 0x1 and reg.exe reads it back.

presets.label: PCA enabled (policy explicit)
presets.description: disabledValue in AppCompat.admx. Equivalent to missing: PCA remains turned on.

entries.name: Recall Snapshot Saving
entries.description: Recall can save snapshots of what you have seen on the screen so you can search and revisit it later. This policy decides whether those snapshots can be saved for the signed-in user.

presets.label: Recall snapshots turned off
presets.description: Snapshots are not saved for Recall, and previously saved snapshots are deleted when this policy is enabled.

presets.label: Users can choose to save Recall snapshots
presets.description: This policy does not block snapshot saving, so the user can choose whether to save snapshots for Recall when the feature is available.

entries.name: Disable Resume for Current User
entries.description: Resume lets you start on one device and continue on this PC. This tweak turns off that current-user Resume setting.

presets.label: Resume disabled
presets.description: Observed Settings and app value for turning the current-user Resume setting off.

presets.label: Resume enabled
presets.description: Observed Settings value for turning the current-user Resume setting on.

entries.name: Resultant Set of Policy Logging
entries.description: RSoP logging records which Group Policy settings were applied to the PC. Some people turn it off to reduce policy logging, while administrators often keep it on for troubleshooting and auditing.

presets.label: RSoP logging turned off
presets.description: The policy is enabled and RSoP logging is turned off.

presets.label: RSoP logging turned on
presets.description: The policy is disabled and RSoP logging stays on.

entries.name: File Explorer Search Box Suggestions
entries.description: File Explorer can show suggestion pop-ups as you type into its search box, based on past search entries. This policy decides whether those suggestions are available.

presets.label: Search suggestions allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and File Explorer can show recent-query suggestions.

presets.label: Search suggestions disabled
presets.description: File Explorer won't show suggestion pop-ups or store search-box entries for future references.

entries.name: Search History Storage and Display
entries.description: Windows can remember previous search queries and use them to suggest searches later. This policy decides whether that search history is stored and shown for the current user.

presets.label: Search history allowed
presets.description: Previous searches can be stored and used for later search suggestions.

presets.label: Search history disabled
presets.description: Search queries aren't stored in the registry and previous-search suggestions won't appear in the search pane.

entries.name: Windows Sensors
entries.description: Windows can use hardware sensors such as orientation, ambient light, motion, or other environmental sensors. This policy decides whether sensors are allowed.

presets.label: Sensors allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and sensors remain available.

presets.label: Sensors disabled
presets.description: Sensors are blocked by policy.

entries.name: Steps Recorder
entries.description: Steps Recorder can capture user actions and screenshots to help explain a problem. This policy decides whether the feature is available.

presets.label: Steps Recorder allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and Steps Recorder stays enabled.

presets.label: Steps Recorder disabled
presets.description: The policy is enabled and Steps Recorder is turned off.

entries.name: Disable SwitchBack Compatibility Policy
entries.description: SwitchBack is a Windows compatibility feature that lets newer applications receive compatibility fixes originally designed for older OS versions. On a modern Windows 11 system running only current software, this feature usually has no practical effect. This policy disables it.

presets.label: SwitchBack enabled (policy explicit)
presets.description: disabledValue in AppCompat.admx. SwitchBack runs normally. Equivalent to missing.

presets.label: Turn off SwitchBack
presets.description: enabledValue in AppCompat.admx. SwitchBack is disabled. Applications that detect Windows Vista or later no longer receive cross-version compatibility fixes. VM Procmon capture on 2026-03-26 in Win25H2Clean confirmed powershell.exe writes SbEnable=REG_DWORD 0x0 and reg.exe reads it back.

entries.name: Diagnostic Data Change Notifications
entries.description: Windows can notify the user when the diagnostic-data opt-in setting changes. This policy decides whether those notifications are shown.

presets.label: Notification allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and the change notification can be shown.

presets.label: Notification disabled
presets.description: The change notification is blocked by policy.

entries.name: Diagnostic Data Opt-In Settings UI
entries.description: Windows can show controls in Settings that let a user change diagnostic data choices. This policy decides whether that Settings UI stays available.

presets.label: Enable diagnostic data opt-in settings
presets.description: End users can change the device diagnostic settings in the Settings app.

presets.label: Disable diagnostic data opt-in settings
presets.description: Diagnostic data settings are disabled in the Settings app and users cannot change them there.

entries.name: Windows Error Reporting
entries.description: Windows Error Reporting can send information about crashes and failures so Microsoft or an internal server can analyze them. This policy turns that reporting off for the device.

presets.label: Windows Error Reporting disabled
presets.description: Problem information is not sent through Windows Error Reporting, and solution information is not available in Security and Maintenance.

presets.label: Policy not forcing Windows Error Reporting off
presets.description: This specific disable policy is turned off, so the broader ICM policy or Control Panel settings can decide Windows Error Reporting behavior.

entries.name: Windows Location Provider
entries.description: Windows has a built-in location provider that apps and system features can use. This policy decides whether that provider is available.

presets.label: Windows Location Provider allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and the provider remains available.

presets.label: Windows Location Provider disabled
presets.description: The provider is blocked by policy.

entries.name: Turn Off Windows Tips
entries.description: Windows can show popups and onboarding tips that explain features and suggest ways to use the system. People often turn them off when they want a quieter desktop experience.

presets.label: Tips allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and Windows tips are not turned off by this machine policy.

presets.label: Tips turned off by policy
presets.description: Users will no longer see Windows tips.

entries.name: Display of the Last Signed-In Username
entries.description: Windows can show the name of the last person who signed in on the sign-in screen. This setting decides whether that username is shown or hidden.

presets.label: Show the last signed-in username
presets.description: The security option is not enabled, so the last signed-in username can appear at sign-in.

presets.label: Hide the last signed-in username
presets.description: The security option is enabled and the last signed-in username is not shown on the sign-in screen.

entries.name: Start Personalized Site Recommendations
entries.description: Windows 11 Start can surface personalized website suggestions. This device policy hides those recommendations for everyone on the machine.

presets.label: Personalized sites shown
presets.description: Personalized site recommendations remain allowed.

presets.label: Personalized sites hidden
presets.description: Personalized site recommendations are hidden.

entries.name: Start Personalized Site Recommendations (Current User)
entries.description: Windows 11 Start can surface personalized website suggestions. This user policy hides those recommendations just for the current account.

presets.label: Personalized sites shown
presets.description: Personalized site recommendations remain allowed for the current user.

presets.label: Personalized sites hidden
presets.description: Personalized site recommendations are hidden for the current user.

entries.name: Start Menu Recommended Section
entries.description: Windows 11 Start can show a Recommended section with suggested apps and files. This policy lets the device hide that section for everyone.

presets.label: Recommended section shown
presets.description: The section remains visible.

presets.label: Recommended section hidden
presets.description: The section is removed from Start.

entries.name: Start Menu Recommended Section (Current User)
entries.description: Windows 11 Start can show a Recommended section with suggested apps and files. This user policy hides that section just for the current account.

presets.label: Recommended section shown
presets.description: The section remains visible for the current user.

presets.label: Recommended section hidden
presets.description: The section is hidden for the current user.

entries.name: Display of Username During Sign-In
entries.description: After someone enters their credentials, Windows can keep showing the username or hide it. This setting decides whether the username stays visible during that sign-in flow.

presets.label: Keep username visible during sign-in
presets.description: The security option is not enabled, so the username can remain visible during the sign-in flow.

presets.label: Hide username during sign-in
presets.description: The security option is enabled and the username is not displayed after credentials are entered.

entries.name: Advanced Diagnostic Log Collection
entries.description: Windows can collect extra diagnostic logs when advanced diagnostics are involved. This policy decides whether that additional log collection is limited.

presets.label: Do not limit advanced diagnostic logs
presets.description: The policy is disabled and advanced diagnostic logging is not restricted by this setting.

presets.label: Limit advanced diagnostic logs
presets.description: Advanced diagnostic log collection is limited by policy.

entries.name: Diagnostic Dump Collection
entries.description: Windows can collect diagnostic dump data for troubleshooting. This policy decides whether that dump collection is limited.

presets.label: Do not limit dump collection
presets.description: The policy is disabled and dump collection is not restricted by this setting.

presets.label: Limit dump collection
presets.description: Diagnostic dump collection is limited by policy.

entries.name: Recommended Troubleshooting for Known Problems
entries.description: Windows can automatically apply or suggest troubleshooting for known problems. This policy controls how much of that automation is allowed.

presets.label: Do nothing
presets.description: Do not allow users, system features, or Microsoft to apply troubleshooting.

presets.label: Apply critical only
presets.description: Only automatically apply troubleshooting for critical problems by system features and Microsoft.

presets.label: Ask first for other problems
presets.description: Automatically apply critical troubleshooting and notify users about troubleshooting for other problems.

presets.label: Apply and notify
presets.description: Automatically apply troubleshooting for critical and other problems and notify users when troubleshooting solved a problem.

presets.label: Apply silently
presets.description: Automatically apply troubleshooting for critical and other problems without notifying users when it solved a problem.

presets.label: Defer to user
presets.description: Allow the user to choose their own troubleshooting settings.

system.name: System
system.description: Stable kernel-adjacent and Session Manager registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Aero Shake Window Minimizing Gesture
entries.description: Aero Shake is the gesture where you grab a window and shake it to minimize or restore other windows. This policy decides whether that gesture works for the current user.

presets.label: Aero Shake allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and the Aero Shake gesture remains available.

presets.label: Aero Shake blocked
presets.description: The policy is enabled and the Aero Shake gesture is turned off.

entries.name: Automatic Restart on System Failure
entries.description: Windows can automatically restart the PC after a blue screen. Turning that off gives you time to see the crash screen and stop code before the machine reboots.

presets.label: Automatic restart enabled
presets.description: Windows automatically reboots after a system failure.

presets.label: Automatic restart disabled
presets.description: Windows does not automatically reboot after a system failure.

entries.name: Display Blue Screen Parameters
entries.description: This tweak tries to show extra technical parameters on a blue screen. That can help advanced debugging, but most users will not benefit from the extra numbers.

presets.label: Do not display stop error information
presets.description: Microsoft Support documents this CrashControl value as the state that hides the extra stop-error details from the blue screen.

presets.label: Display stop error information
presets.description: Microsoft Support documents this CrashControl value as the state that shows additional stop-error details on the blue screen.

entries.name: Automatic App Archiving
entries.description: Windows can archive infrequently used apps to save space while keeping them restorable later. This policy decides whether that automatic archiving is allowed on the device.

presets.label: Automatic app archiving disabled
presets.description: The system will not archive apps automatically.

presets.label: Automatic app archiving allowed
presets.description: Windows can periodically check for and archive infrequently used apps.

entries.name: Automatic Maintenance
entries.description: Automatic Maintenance runs maintenance work like updates, scans, and housekeeping when Windows thinks the PC is idle. People disable it when they want tighter control over when maintenance runs.

entries.name: Background Group Policy Refresh
entries.description: Windows normally refreshes Group Policy in the background while the system is being used. This policy lets the device wait until logoff before applying those updates.

entries.name: Clipboard History and Cross-Device Clipboard Sync
entries.description: Windows can keep a history of copied items and can sync clipboard data across devices. These two policy values decide whether those features are allowed.

entries.name: RDP Clipboard Redirection
entries.description: Remote Desktop can let text and files move between your local clipboard and the remote machine. This policy controls whether that copy and paste bridge is allowed.

presets.label: Clipboard redirection allowed
presets.description: Clipboard sharing between local and remote sessions is allowed.

presets.label: Clipboard redirection blocked
presets.description: Clipboard sharing between local and remote sessions is blocked.

entries.name: Fullscreen Optimizations
entries.description: Fullscreen Optimizations is a Windows feature that tries to blend fullscreen-style game performance with some modern desktop and presentation behavior. People usually turn it off only when a specific game behaves badly with it.

entries.name: Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting
entries.description: Windows includes built-in game recording and broadcasting features. This policy decides whether those features are allowed on the device.

presets.label: Game recording disabled
presets.description: Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting are not allowed by policy.

presets.label: Game recording allowed
presets.description: Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting are allowed.

entries.name: Wallpaper JPEG Import Quality
entries.description: Windows can reduce the quality of JPEG images when you set them as wallpaper. People change this when they want the wallpaper to stay as sharp as possible.

entries.name: Search Highlights
entries.description: Search Highlights are the dynamic bits Windows shows in the search area, such as seasonal or suggested content. This policy decides whether those highlights are allowed.

presets.label: Disabled
presets.description: Search Highlights are turned off.

presets.label: Enabled
presets.description: Search Highlights are explicitly allowed.

entries.name: Remote Windows Search Queries
entries.description: Windows Search can let other computers query this PC's search index over the network. This policy decides whether that remote index use is allowed.

presets.label: Remote queries allowed
presets.description: Client search requests can use this computer's search index.

presets.label: Remote queries blocked
presets.description: Clients cannot query this computer's index remotely.

entries.name: Web Results in Windows Search
entries.description: Windows Search can send queries to the web and show web results in the search experience. This policy decides whether that web-connected behavior is allowed.

presets.label: Web results disabled
presets.description: Search does not perform web queries and does not display web results.

presets.label: Web results allowed
presets.description: Search can perform web queries and display web results.

entries.name: Startup Program Delay
entries.description: Windows can stagger startup apps instead of launching them all immediately. People disable the delay when they want login to feel quicker, but that can also make startup load spike harder.

entries.name: DWM Overlay Minimum FPS Check
entries.description: Windows can use hardware overlays for some content, and one of the checks looks at how fast the surface is animating. This setting turns that minimum-FPS check off.

entries.name: Game Mode
entries.description: Game Mode is Windows' built-in gaming feature that tries to reduce interruptions and prioritize the current game. Most users either leave it on or benchmark it for a specific game.

presets.label: Game Mode disabled
presets.description: Observed runtime state for AutoGameModeEnabled on this build. Guest-side Procmon captured SystemSettings.exe querying the Administrator hive with Data:0 in a reversible capture.

presets.label: Game Mode enabled
presets.description: Observed runtime state for AutoGameModeEnabled on this build. Guest-side Procmon captured SystemSettings.exe querying the Administrator hive with Data:1 in a reversible capture.

entries.name: Indexing of Encrypted Files
entries.description: Windows Search can be told to index encrypted files so their contents are searchable. That can make searching easier, but it also means Windows needs to process decrypted content during indexing.

presets.label: Do not index encrypted files
presets.description: Search components are expected not to index encrypted items or encrypted stores.

presets.label: Index encrypted files
presets.description: Indexing attempts to decrypt and index encrypted content while still respecting access restrictions.

entries.name: Executive Additional Worker Threads
entries.description: These values appear to control extra executive worker threads for internal critical and delayed work queues. They are low-level kernel-adjacent knobs and are being tracked as research only.

entries.name: Graphics TDR DDI Delay
entries.description: Windows gives graphics-driver threads a limited amount of time to leave the driver during TDR recovery. This setting controls that delay.

entries.name: Graphics TDR Delay
entries.description: Windows uses TDR to detect when the GPU takes too long to respond. This setting controls the main timeout threshold before recovery starts.

entries.name: Graphics TDR Level
entries.description: Windows can react to GPU timeouts in different ways, such as disabling detection or recovering on timeout. This setting controls that recovery mode.

presets.label: Recover on timeout
presets.description: Recover on timeout using the Microsoft-documented default TDR level.

presets.label: Detection disabled
presets.description: Timeout detection is disabled.

presets.label: Bugcheck on timeout
presets.description: Windows bug-checks on a detected timeout instead of recovering.

presets.label: Recover to VGA
presets.description: Recover to VGA; Microsoft notes this path is not implemented.

entries.name: Graphics TDR Limit Count
entries.description: Windows keeps track of how many GPU hangs occur within the TDR time window. This setting controls that count threshold.

entries.name: Graphics TDR Limit Time
entries.description: Windows measures GPU hang events within a time window when deciding how to respond to repeated timeouts. This setting controls that time window.

entries.name: Threaded DPCs
entries.description: Threaded DPCs let some kernel deferred work run in a way that can reduce system latency compared with ordinary DPCs. Most normal systems should leave this enabled.

presets.label: Threaded DPCs disabled
presets.description: Threaded DPCs run as ordinary DPCs instead.

presets.label: Threaded DPCs enabled
presets.description: Threaded DPCs stay enabled, which is the documented normal behavior.

entries.name: Disable Exception Chain Validation
entries.description: DisableExceptionChainValidation is a low-level Session Manager Kernel registry value tied to exception-chain policy handling during early boot.

entries.name: Clear Page File at Shutdown
entries.description: Windows can wipe the page file when the PC shuts down. This can reduce leftover data on disk, but it also makes shutdown take longer.

presets.label: Do not clear page file
presets.description: Windows does not wipe the page file during shutdown.

presets.label: Clear page file at shutdown
presets.description: Windows wipes the page file during shutdown.

entries.name: Disable Paging Executive
entries.description: This setting was used for older tracing and diagnosis scenarios to keep some kernel-mode code and drivers in RAM instead of letting Windows page them out to disk. Microsoft says Windows 8 and newer systems do not need this change.

presets.label: Paging executive allowed
presets.description: The special tracing-oriented nonpaged behavior is turned off.

presets.label: Paging executive disabled
presets.description: Drivers and kernel-mode system code are kept from being paged to disk for the documented diagnosis and tracing scenarios.

entries.name: Large System Cache
entries.description: Windows historically had a switch between favoring normal applications and favoring a larger system cache. Most normal users should leave this alone on modern systems.

presets.label: Optimize for applications
presets.description: The historical semantics exposed by Win32_OperatingSystem say memory is optimized for applications.

presets.label: Optimize for system performance
presets.description: The historical semantics exposed by Win32_OperatingSystem say memory is optimized for system performance.

entries.name: Nonpaged Pool Size
entries.description: Nonpaged pool is kernel memory that must always stay resident in RAM. This is a low-level legacy tuning area that normal users should not adjust manually.

entries.name: Paged Pool Size
entries.description: Paged pool is kernel memory that Windows can page out when needed. This is a legacy low-level memory tuning area that most people should never touch manually.

presets.label: Default paged pool size
presets.description: The default reset value captured in Microsoft Q&A.

presets.label: Maximum paged pool for a specific older server issue
presets.description: Older Microsoft troubleshooting guidance uses 0xFFFFFFFF to allocate the maximum paged pool for a specific problem scenario.

entries.name: Registry Size Limit / Registry Quota
entries.description: Windows historically exposed a registry size limit tied to paged-pool memory. Modern systems normally manage this automatically, so the safest reset is to return the published control to automatic sizing.

entries.name: NTFS 8.3 Short Name Creation
entries.description: NTFS can create old-style short file names for compatibility. Disabling them can reduce some filesystem overhead, but some legacy software still expects those short names to exist.

presets.label: Per-volume behavior
presets.description: Short-name creation is controlled per volume and this is the documented default mode.

presets.label: Enable on all volumes
presets.description: NTFS creates 8.3 short names on all volumes.

presets.label: Disable on all volumes
presets.description: NTFS does not create 8.3 short names on any volume.

presets.label: Disable on all data volumes
presets.description: Short names are created only on the system volume and disabled on data volumes.

entries.name: NTFS Last Access Time Updates
entries.description: Windows can update a file or directory's last-access timestamp when it is accessed. Disabling these updates can reduce some disk overhead, but software that depends on last-access data can lose that signal.

presets.label: Last-access updates disabled
presets.description: Windows does not update last-access timestamps on NTFS volumes.

presets.label: Last-access updates enabled
presets.description: Windows records last-access timestamp updates on NTFS volumes.

entries.name: Win32 Long Paths
entries.description: Windows normally keeps many apps limited to shorter file paths. This setting allows long paths for apps that are built to support them.

presets.label: Long paths disabled
presets.description: Win32 long paths are not enabled through this setting.

presets.label: Long paths enabled
presets.description: Long-path-aware applications can access paths beyond the normal 260-character limit.

entries.name: NTFS Memory Usage
entries.description: NTFS has an internal memory-usage tuning that affects its cache behavior. Most people should leave it at the default unless they have a proven file-server style workload.

presets.label: Default NTFS memory usage
presets.description: NTFS uses the default amount of paged-pool memory.

presets.label: Raised NTFS memory usage
presets.description: NTFS increases its lookaside lists and memory thresholds.

entries.name: NTFS MFT Zone Reservation
entries.description: NTFS reserves some space for the master file table so it can grow with less fragmentation. This setting controls how large that reserved area is.

presets.label: Default minimum reservation
presets.description: Use the default minimum MFT zone size.

presets.label: Larger reservation
presets.description: Reserve a larger MFT zone for workloads with many small files.

presets.label: Much larger reservation
presets.description: Reserve a much larger MFT zone for more extreme file-count workloads.

presets.label: Maximum reservation
presets.description: Reserve the largest supported MFT zone size.

entries.name: Foreground Scheduling Priority / Win32PrioritySeparation
entries.description: This setting changes how Windows gives extra CPU time to the foreground application compared with background work. It is a low-level scheduler setting, not a normal everyday tweak.

presets.label: Observed Win25H2Clean baseline
presets.description: The current 25H2 VM baseline read back Win32PrioritySeparation = 2 before the app profile was applied. This is an observed runtime state, not a claim about the full raw bitmask semantics.

presets.label: Observed app profile
presets.description: The current app writes 38 (0x26), and the Win25H2Clean VM confirmed that observed state under real rebooted runs. This record does not claim that Microsoft publishes the full raw 0x26 bit semantics.

entries.name: Reliability Event Timestamping
entries.description: Windows can timestamp reliability events on a cadence. This setting controls whether that timestamping behavior runs for the machine.

entries.name: Service Shutdown Timeout
entries.description: Windows waits a set amount of time for a service to stop cleanly during shutdown. Lowering that timeout can make shutdown finish faster, but it gives services less time to flush state and clean up.

presets.label: Observed Win25H2Clean baseline
presets.description: The current Win25H2Clean VM waits 5 seconds before terminating an unresponsive service during shutdown.

presets.label: Current app profile
presets.description: The app shortens the service shutdown timeout to 2.5 seconds.

visibility.name: Visibility
visibility.description: Validated Visibility registry research cards surfaced directly from research records.

entries.name: Acrylic Blur on the Logon Background
entries.description: Windows can blur the logon background with an acrylic effect. This policy decides whether that blur is turned off so the background stays clear.

entries.name: Common Control and Window Animations
entries.description: Windows can animate common controls and some window transitions. This policy decides whether those animations are turned off for the current user.

presets.label: Animations allowed
presets.description: The policy is disabled and common control and window animations remain on.

presets.label: Animations turned off
presets.description: The policy is enabled and common control and window animations are turned off for the current user.

entries.name: First Sign-In Animation
entries.description: Windows can show a first sign-in animation and, for Microsoft-account users, an opt-in prompt for services the first time someone signs in. This policy decides whether that first-run experience is shown.

presets.label: Show the first sign-in animation
presets.description: The policy is enabled, so users see the first sign-in animation and Microsoft-account users see the services opt-in prompt.

presets.label: Skip the first sign-in animation
presets.description: The policy is disabled, so users do not see the animation and Microsoft-account users do not see the services opt-in prompt.

entries.name: Lock Screen Camera Access
entries.description: Windows can allow a camera to be used directly from the lock screen. This policy decides whether that lock-screen camera access can be enabled.

entries.name: Changing the Lock Screen and Logon Image
entries.description: Windows normally lets users change the lock-screen and logon background image. This policy decides whether users are allowed to change those images.
